biography.plain_text: Robert Bishop is an American investment manager who founded Impala Asset Management after serving as chief investment officer at Soros Fund Management. Based in Palm Beach, he developed a specialist practice in industrial and commodity-related shares. He subsequently returned outside investors' capital and converted Impala into a family office managing private wealth.

long_biography.plain_text:
Investment manager Robert Bishop has used shareholder campaigns to press for changes inside companies. At Harley-Davidson, his firm nominated two directors with experience in motor racing, television and the automotive industry. Bishop wanted them to influence strategy and the selection of a new chief executive, following concerns about the company's performance.

His university giving has recognised a former teacher. Having studied military sociology under Charles Moskos at Northwestern, Bishop endowed a chair bearing the professor's name. The first holder was economist Martin Eichenbaum, whose research examined economic fluctuations, including the causes and consequences of changing exchange rates.
